newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Scent of a president on sale in Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: Scent of a president on sale in Turkmenistan.

text.p: Shops in Ashgabat this month have started selling a French-made scent for men named after Turkmenistan's strongman leader Saparmurat Niyazov, the focus of an expanding personality cult.
The scent is named "Turkmenbashi", or "leader of the Turkmens", the title by which Niyazov is commonly known.
Niyazov stares at potential buyers from a portrait on the scent's packaging, with "France" printed neatly underneath, and sells for about $40 -- double the desert nation's average monthly salary.
Those unable to afford this scent of a man will still have plenty of opportunities to view his likeness.

Portraits of Niyazov, Turkmenistan's former Communist Party boss and who tolerates no dissent, are placed on most street corners. Farms, military units and a port town on the Caspian Sea have been named after the Turkmen leader.
Yoghurt with Niyazov's face printed on each carton went on sale in Ashgabat recently. A variety of dahlia has also been named "Turkmenbashi".
